Volkswirtschaftlicher Lagebericht

Quarterly Report to the State Ministry — Q2 1924
Ref. F 331/24  ·  Berlin, 14 April 1924  ·  Print run: 12 copies

The economic situation of the Free State remains strained. After four consecutive years of crisis, the figures below show a continued contraction of the real economy, falling real wages, and an unemployment rate many times above pre-war levels. The Ministry hereby submits to the State Ministry its quarterly overview of the principal economic indicators.

I.Overall Economic Development

Real gross domestic product fell 4.8 % against the previous year, the fourth consecutive decline. Income per capita has fallen 16.8 % since its 1931 peak. Heavy industry has been hit hardest, with output collapsing 9.1 % within the year. (see Fig. 1 and 2)

Abb. 2 — Bruttoinlandsprodukt je Kopfin RM
falling

II.Prices

The wholesale price index fell 2.1 % over the reporting period; the Ministry observes a continued deflation. Nonetheless, the memory of the currency collapse remains active among the population, further dampening savings behaviour and lending. (see Fig. 3)

Abb. 3 — Großhandelspreisindex1924 = 100
deflationary
Abb. 3b — InflationsrateVeränderung ggü. Vorjahr, in %
deflationary

III.Labour Market

Unemployment has reached a new high of 21.7 %; 2.85 million persons are registered with the labour exchanges. The increase has been uninterrupted since 1931 and has struck heavy industry hardest. (see Fig. 4)

VI.Special Remarks

—Banking sector strained: Regional savings banks report increased withdrawal pressure; the Ministry continues to monitor the situation.
—Estate agriculture in crisis: East Elbian landholders are petitioning for relief; a separate report from the Agriculture Division will follow.

VII.Sectors of the Reich Economy

The following survey sets out the condition of the principal branches of the national economy, together with an assessment of production trend, employment, contribution to output, indebtedness and profitability. (see Table 3)

Table 3 — Survey of Economic Sectors
Sector Production Employed Output Debt Profitability
Heavy Industry slowing 1.9M 12 % high negative
Heavy industry concerned primarily with the extraction of coal, iron, and the manufacture of steel in the Ruhr Valley and Upper Silesia. Cartelization is high in this sector.
Mood: disgruntled
The political interests of this group are represented by the DNVP and DVP.
Export Industry steady 2.4M 18 % moderate thin
The industry which produces machinery, chemicals, and electrotechnics primarily sold abroad. The performance of this sector is sensitive to world trade as well as foreign tariffs.
Mood: content
The political interests of this group are represented by the DVP and DDP.
Light Industry steady 2.0M 15 % moderate thin
Light industry encompasses consumer good production for the domestic market, including textiles, clothing, and foodstuffs. It is significantly influenced by domestic purchasing power.
Mood: content
The political interests of this group are represented by the DDP, and to a smaller extent, Z.
Estate Agriculture contracting 1.8M 5 % very high negative
The grain estates east of the Elbe, which are almost permanently unprofitable. Most estates are deeply mortgaged and dependent on the tariff to prevent cheap imports from competing with their agricultural output.
Mood: desperate
Peasant Agriculture steady 7.5M 10 % high squeezed
Subsistence agriculture in Germany consists of farms which specialize in dairying, livestock, and other mixed crops.
Mood: anxious
Mittelstand slowing 3.5M 12 % rising weak
Artisans, shopkeepers, and small traders, which are derogatorily called the petite bourgeois. Oftentimes crowded by the cooperatives and big industry.
Mood: anxious
Construction expanding 1.0M 5 % moderate negative
The building trades which are kept afloat by public housing programmes and municipal contracts with the state.
